noise: A shared CI runner is a noisy host. Other tenants share the physical machine and nothing in the job can see them, and the two runs here landed on different CPU models. A number from it is a comparison between halves of one job, not an absolute, and the one accepted half below is a single sample with no spread.
ifb: Available from the runner image's stock modules on both runs: modprobe ifb sch_netem sch_tbf sch_ingress cls_u32 act_mirred succeeded on the first try (linux-modules-extra was not needed), and an ifb device came up inside a fresh network namespace. The middlebox shaped every half: emulator calibration 9.533-9.575 Mbit/s against the configured 10.0, and solo windows 9.553-9.564 Mbit/s.

accepted_half.reading: One uncapped half from one run on one shared host, with no capped half beside it, so it is not a pair and not #610's result. It is read only beside #481's Lima uncapped half (4.723 Mbit/s, 49%, Jain 0.961), which it resembles. Its contended window was 120.102 s, longer than its 120.000 s stream. It passed the coverage check only because the first interval reached back across the window's opening (see refusal.why_some_windows_pass), which is the same clock mismatch hidden rather than absent.

refusal.check: benchmarks/lib/competitor.py competitor_bytes_over(): the competing flow's per-interval stream must cover the whole window the receiver's total is spread across.
refusal.observed: In every refused window the stream was missing the window's first N seconds, where N is between 0.100 and 0.169 s in the first run and 0.143 and 0.149 s in the diagnostic run.
refusal.cause: The window the stream is laid into is the RECEIVER's, and the stream is the SENDER's. _measured_intervals() takes the window's length from end.sum_received.seconds and lays the client's interval stream into it with the last interval's end on the window's end. On iperf 3.21 the client's stream covers exactly the sender's measured window: 120 intervals of about 1.000 s from 0.0001, the last ending at end.sum_sent.seconds (diagnostic-run-42948066440/clock_comparison.json, sender_last_interval_end == sum_sent_seconds in all four kept phases). sum_received.seconds is the server's own measured time, and it ends when the server learns the test is over. It is longer by the time the tail of the flow takes to drain the 1-BDP queue and cross the 50 ms one-way delay: receiver_minus_sender_seconds was 0.143383 and 0.149431 beside VTOP and 0.169774 and 0.190803 alone. Each refused window's hole equals that difference exactly: 0.143 and 0.149 s in the diagnostic run's logs. The same report's end.streams[0].receiver.seconds is the sender's 120.000653, not the receiver's 120.144036, which shows the two clocks side by side. Bytes agree: in one refused window sum_received.bytes equals sum_sent.bytes (112066560), so the receiver's longer clock is the same bytes arriving later, not more measuring.
refusal.why_some_windows_pass: The check passes when the first measured interval's 'seconds' reaches back past the window's opening, because _measured_intervals() clamps an entry's beginning to 0 and so covers the hole. That is the iperf 3.16 behaviour the test fixture models: the first entry straddles the omit restart. On iperf 3.21 whether it straddles depends on how the omit timer and the interval timer race at the 3 s mark. The server's own report shows that race (one refused window's first measured server line is '1.00-1.00 sec 896 KBytes'). Every refused window's first sender interval is about 1.000 s long (clock_comparison.json, sender_first_interval). The accepted uncapped half (contended window 120.102 s) and #481's Lima runs (120.142 s and 120.105 s, 120 intervals each) could only have passed with a straddling first entry. That is inferred, not observed: a window that passes keeps no raw report.
refusal.not_the_cause: Not ifb, netem or the cap: calibration and solo windows were normal in every half. Not a missing final interval line: every report has all 120 measured intervals, the last ending at sum_sent.seconds. Not buffering: the accepted half's sync spread was 0.002 s.
refusal.proposed_fix: Place the stream on its own clock: take the origin and the coverage window from end.sum_sent.seconds (the sender's measured window, which on 3.21 is the stream's own last end) rather than from end.sum_received.seconds. Keep the goodput as the receiver's bytes over the receiver's seconds. The receiver's extra 0.10-0.19 s is the queue draining after the sender stopped: the competitor sends nothing in it, so it is not part of the contended window, and the proportional spread already assumes a gap of one queue's worth between sender and receiver. The guarantee holds: a hole inside the sender's own window is still refused. This is proposed, not applied, because it also moves where close() places the window (its length, the solo-tail check and the latest-opening bound) by the same 0.10-0.19 s, and that change wants its own review.
refusal.why_not_filled_in: The check is the harness's own guard against overstating fairness, so it is not weakened to get a number.
